AP News, Wed 22 Jul 2026 05:18 GMT — Rubio warned Asian leaders in Manila that Iran's demand to control and collect tolls in the Strait of Hormuz would threaten the world economy and set a precedent repeatable elsewhere. Spoke at start of annual ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting. "We're with ASEAN 100%." Also met Quad counterparts (Australia, India, Japan) on maritime/transnational security. New British Foreign Secretary [Miliband] due to meet Rubio Wednesday. Backdrop: China-Philippines clash at Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin).
Rubio verbatim (via CNA, channelnewsasia.com/world/iran-strait-hormuz-rubio-asean-dangerous-precedent-6269826): "If we create a precedent in the Middle East where a nation-state can decide to control an international waterway, charge a toll, and blow up your ships if you don't pay, we have created a very dangerous precedent that will repeat itself in other parts of the world, including this region." "There is a fundamental principle about freedom of navigation that is threatened."
Rubio-Wang Yi bilateral held Wednesday on the sidelines (per SCMP/Reuters pool). Rubio (UPI upi.com/.../6571784704435): US "remains open and willing to engage in positive, constructive negotiations... so long as the commitments that are made are kept" but Iran "not serious." NOTE: SCMP/Reuters/UPI/CNA used for cross-ref only — cite AP + CNA (approved) in copy.
